# CODING-HERMES-DIRECTOR — HARNESS API ENDPOINT CONTRACT
``` DOC : contracts/ENDPOINTS.md REV : 1.1 (R31 revision pass 2026-11-09). Delta vs 1.0: §4.2 carries the seven-value kind enum and the single non-member error contract; §4.4 non-member wake target collapsed into 404 not_found; §5 table aligned one-to-one with VOL-C §3.6 (the bare `403 forbidden` row is deleted — unknown and unreadable room are indistinguishable `404 not_found`, cause in audit only). DATE : 2026-11-09 IMPLEMENTS: DESIGN.md v2 CT-02/CT-03/CT-05/CT-06/CT-07, §3.3, §4.4, §6 STATUS : CONTRACT TO BUILD AGAINST. No server exists yet; every shape here is normative for the M2+ milestones. Base URL for all paths below: the harness service (its per-lane gateway_url target, FACT-27). All bodies are JSON (application/json). ```
---

## 1. Conventions
- **Envelope.** Every error response uses: ```json { "error": { "code": "bad_request", "message": "human-readable", "detail": {} } } ``` - **Idempotency.** Mutating endpoints accept an optional `dedupe_key` (string). A replayed `dedupe_key` returns the original response with `200` (not `201`) and writes nothing. - **Timestamps** are RFC 3339 UTC strings. - **DuckBrain writes** go through the harness's own authenticated surface; key names in §7 per endpoint.

## 2. Auth model (VP)
Two principal classes:
- **VP (virtual principal)** — the owner or a surface the owner delegates (web UI, CLI on the owner's host, approved webhooks). Authenticated by a VP token (operator-provisioned, like DuckBrain role tokens, FACT-20). - **Internal agents** — director/manager/supervisor sessions, authenticated by their role tokens.
**Rule (normative):** - VP callers are **default-allow**: a valid VP token grants every harness endpoint in this document (the owner may post to any room, wake anyone, read anything, verify, and bump). - Internal agents are **default-deny for every endpoint in this document** — even with a valid agent token, a request that claims VP identity (`as: "vp"` or a VP token presented by an agent principal) is refused `403 vp_identity_misuse` and counted as an integrity violation (DESIGN §6.3). Agents reach rooms only via CT-05 DuckBrain writes with their own role token; they never call the harness API as VP. - Scheduler callbacks authenticate with the scheduler's own credential (mutating credential held only by the harness service and scheduler, §6.1); auth failure is terminal, no retry flood (FACT-12).
## 3. Signal ingress

### 3.1 `POST /v1/signals` — API/webhook entry point
External systems (webhook, CI, another fleet component) push a signal; the harness turns it into a room message and/or a wake.
Request: ```json { "source": "ci-webhook", // caller-chosen source id "type": "board-row|alert|external-event", "payload": { "board_row": "row-42" }, "target_room": "obj-fleet", // existing room "as": "vp", // literal; VP-only endpoint "dedupe_key": "gh-run-1234" } ``` Response `202`: ```json { "signal_id": "sig-20261107-1530-x9y2", "accepted": true, "message_seq": 41, "wakes": ["mgr-infra"] } ``` Writes: message at `chd/room/<target_room>/<seq>` (`from: "signal:<source>"`), wake decisions recorded in the send manifest (§7). Errors: `400` malformed, `401` unauthenticated, `403` non-VP caller, `404` unknown room, `409` dedupe replay (only when body differs), `429` gateway at `max_inflight` (signal logged, wake queued, not lost), `503` DuckBrain down (§5.3: nothing dispatches).

### 3.2 MCP tool surface
Exposed to owner-side MCP clients; each tool is a thin wrapper on an endpoint below (same request/response shapes, same auth):
| MCP tool | Backing endpoint | |----------|------------------| | `chd_create_room` | `POST /v1/rooms` | | `chd_post_message` | `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages` | | `chd_reply` | `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages/{seq}/replies` | | `chd_wake` | `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages/{seq}/wake` | | `chd_read_room` | `GET /v1/rooms/{room}/messages` | | `chd_verify_report` | `POST /v1/reports/verify` | | `chd_status` | `GET /v1/status` |
MCP exposure rides Muster or Hermes-native MCP (UQ-4/OQ-4); the tool names and payloads above are the stable part of the contract.

### 3.3 CLI verbs
``` chd rooms -> GET /v1/status chd rooms create --kind objective ... -> POST /v1/rooms chd post <room> --body "..." [--to X] -> POST /v1/rooms/<room>/messages chd reply <room> <seq> --body "..." -> POST /v1/rooms/<room>/messages/<seq>/replies chd wake <room> <seq> --agent mgr-infra -> POST /v1/rooms/<room>/messages/<seq>/wake chd read <room> [--since <seq>] [--thread <seq>] -> GET /v1/rooms/<room>/messages chd verify <report-id> -> POST /v1/reports/verify ``` CLI runs on the owner's host and authenticates as VP (default-allow).

### 3.4 Scheduler-callback lane contract (CT-02/CT-03, RL-1)
The harness registers NORMAL scheduler cooldown lanes whose per-lane `gateway_url` is the harness API (FACT-27). When a lane fires, the scheduler POSTs the tick here:
`POST /v1/cycle` ```json { "cycle": "director-sync", // or "manager-<agent-id>" "lane": "director-sync-lane", "namespace": "director", "ts": "2026-11-07T18:00:00Z", "dedupe_key": "tick-20261107-1800-director-sync" } ``` Response `200` (the scheduler's tick completes cleanly): ```json { "cycle": "director-sync", "accepted": true, "sends_composed": 3, "sends_queued": 1, "bump_requests": 3 } ``` Behavior: the harness calls itself back into its cycle path — compose sends under per-gateway `max_inflight`, request admission ONLY via the scheduler bump API `POST /api/v1/projects/{name}/bump` (FACT-14) or the owner-approved `wake_once` extension (Q-6) — and returns 2xx. It never spawns directly (R-018) and never overrides admission (R-003). Writes: `chd/send/<send-id>/manifest` per composed send. Errors: `401` callback not from the scheduler, `400` unknown cycle, `429` nothing dispatched (all sends queued — still 2xx to the scheduler when the callback itself is valid; 429 is reserved for other callers). With zero trigger lanes registered this endpoint is never called and the harness emits no gateway traffic (R-012).
## 4. Room ops

### 4.1 `POST /v1/rooms` — create room (VP)
Request: ```json { "id": "obj-fleet", "kind": "objective", "participants": ["director", "mgr-infra", "mgr-fleet-ops"], "opening_post": { "from": "director", "kind": "directive", "body": "..." }, "dedupe_key": "obj-fleet" } ``` Response `201`: ```json { "room": "obj-fleet", "kind": "objective", "seq": 1, "created": true } ``` Validation: kind-consistent membership (§1.3 DATA-MODEL); `space` refused `403 registry_unjustified` when a member has no registry entry (CT-09). Writes: `chd/room/<id>/1` (opening post).

### 4.2 `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages` — post message (VP or agent surface)
`kind` is one of the complete seven-value enum `msg | question | status | directive | task | report | incident` (R31-003; identical in VOL-B §3.1 and VOL-C §3.6). Per-role/per-room legality is the single VOL-C §3.6 table (VOLC-066): a prohibited kind is refused `403 kind_not_allowed` naming `{kind, room_kind, role}`.
Request: ```json { "from": "owner", "to": "mgr-infra", // agent id | "group" | "@mgr-infra" "kind": "msg", "body": "prioritize the crier red main", "attach": [], "dedupe_key": "owner-177" } ``` Response `201`: ```json { "room": "obj-fleet", "seq": 42, "key": "chd/room/obj-fleet/42", "wakes": ["mgr-infra"] } ``` Semantics: `from: "owner"` posts are **not** echoed back to the owner (no self-echo, RL-6). `to` decides wakes only; the log is visible to every member. Writes: `chd/room/<room>/<seq>`. Non-member contract (single, all doors — R31-002): a room that does not exist **or** is not readable by the caller returns one `404 not_found` with the identical body shape in both cases — existence and membership are deliberately indistinguishable; the detailed denial cause is written to the audit record only (VOLC-064). Errors: `403 identity_mismatch` (owner-id spoofing by a non-owner principal, VOLC-001); `403 kind_not_allowed` (§3.6 legality, VOL-C); `404 not_found` (unknown or unreadable room, per the non-member contract above); `429` gateway at `max_inflight` (message persisted, wake queued — the log is indifferent to wake timing). The complete code table is §5.

### 4.3 `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages/{seq}/replies` — reply into a thread
Request: ```json { "from": "mgr-infra", "to": "group", "body": "on it — details tonight", "dedupe_key": "r-42-1" } ``` Response `201`: ```json { "room": "obj-fleet", "seq": 43, "thread": 42, "key": "chd/room/obj-fleet/43", "wakes": ["director"] } ``` The new message carries `thread: <seq>`. Threads are reads over the same log — no separate storage.

### 4.4 `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages/{seq}/wake` — @-wake (VP)
Force a single-agent wake pointing at a message that stays searchable in the log (RL-6). Request: ```json { "agent": "mgr-infra", "as": "vp", "note": "see this now" } ``` Response `202`: ```json { "woken": ["mgr-infra"], "queued": false, "mode": "REUSE" } ``` `mode` is one of the only two delivery modes (CT-04): the message lands as the next turn of the bonded session (REUSE) or opens a fresh session (NEW) per the agent's `reuse_policy`. Target must be a member of the room: an unknown **or** non-member agent returns one `404 not_found` — existence and membership are indistinguishable (same non-member contract as §4.2, R31-002); the denial cause is recorded in the audit record only. Subject to per-gateway limits: at capacity the wake queues and the response is `202 {queued: true}`.

### 4.5 `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/bump` — bump + `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/missing-replies/notify`
**Bump** (VP): re-paces the room's outstanding sends — for each open send in the room, request one scheduler admission via bump (FACT-14): ```json { "as": "vp", "scope": "all-open-sends" } ``` Response `200`: ```json { "room": "obj-fleet", "bumped": 2, "already_queued": 1 } ```
**Missing-reply notify** (VP or the verify loop): compute members who were addressed (`to:` them, or `group`) since `since_seq` and have no later message in the room, then wake them: ```json { "since_seq": 40, "as": "vp" } ``` Response `200`: ```json { "room": "obj-fleet", "missing": ["mgr-fleet-ops"], "notified": ["mgr-fleet-ops"], "ladder_started": [] } ``` Agents already inside the re-prompt ladder (§5.1) are reported in `ladder_started` instead of being double-woken. Writes: wakes recorded in `chd/send/<send-id>/manifest` rows; no room write unless a wake message is composed.

### 4.6 `POST /v1/reports/verify` — report verification (CT-06)
Idempotent re-check of a report against its send.
Request: ```json { "report_id": "r-20261107-1531-k4m8" } ``` or, to verify a raw report v3 before posting: ```json { "report": { "schema_version": 3, "envelope": { "id": "r-20261107-1531-k4m8", "send_id": "s-20261107-1530-a1b2", "attempt_id": "at-20261107-1530-c3d4", "request_ref": "/chd/room/task-crier-42/m000000000041", "session_ref": {"mode":"REUSE", "session_key":"chd-sess-sup-crier"}, "status": "done", "summary": "...", "content_ref": "/chd/report/s-20261107-1530-a1b2/r-20261107-1531-k4m8", "content_digest": "sha256:...", "ingest_ts": "service-stamped", "assignment": {"required_content":"free_form", "validation_policy":"none", "completion_policy":"manager_reported"} }, "content": {"class":"free_form", "text":"..."} } } ``` Response `200`: ```json { "report_id": "r-20261107-1531-k4m8", "verdict": "verified", // verified | no_report | bad_report | failed "checks": { "schema_valid": true, "freshness": true, // ingest_ts >= dispatch_ts for same attempt "artifacts_present": true, "artifact_sampled": true // harness samples existence (M5) }, "send_closed": true } ``` Failure shapes: `verdict: "bad_report"` with `checks.freshness: false` and `reason: "stale"` when the v3 freshness rule (DATA-MODEL §1.5) fails; `reason: "done_without_artifacts"`; or `reason: "wrong_request"|"attempt_mismatch"`. Writes: outcome recorded in the send manifest; a `bad_report` starts the §5.1 ladder. Errors: `404` unknown report/send, `422 schema_unsupported|schema_validation|dataset_row_invalid` for v3 schema negotiation/content/row failures, `503` DuckBrain down (cannot read the report message → no verdict is manufactured).

### 4.7 `GET /v1/rooms/{room}/messages` — UI read endpoint
Read-scoped room log for the web UI and `chd read`. Query params: `since` (seq), `thread` (root seq), `limit` (1–500, default 100).
Response `200`: ```json { "room": "obj-fleet", "messages": [ { "seq": 41, "from": "director", "to": "group", "kind": "directive", "body": "...", "thread": null, "attach": [], "ts": "..." } ], "next_since": 42 } ``` Auth: VP tokens read anything. UI read-only tokens (§6.1 supervisor tier) read only rooms their agent is a member of — read scoping per §4.6/§6.2: a caller that cannot name a room gets `404` (not `403`, so key names do not leak). Errors: `404` unknown/unreadable room, `400` bad `limit`.

### 4.9 Ticket operations (controller-routed, boardctl-compatible)
Tickets are shared control-plane state. These endpoints are exposed to the same principal classes as `chd_ticket_*` MCP tools; boardctl uses these APIs rather than a local authoritative board. All mutations require the controller CAS token described below and use the `TicketRecord` schema in `contracts/DATA-MODEL.md §1.9`.
#### `POST /v1/tickets` / `chd_ticket_create`
Request: ```json { "request_id": "req-rel-412", "ticket_id": "REL-412", "title": "Release readiness pack", "kind": "epic", "workflow": {"workflow_id":"chd.objective", "version":1, "machine_ref":"build-spec/state-machines.json#/machines/0"}, "parent_id": null, "depends_on": [], "accountable_owner": "director", "assignees": ["mgr-infra"], "watchers": ["vp"], "criteria": [{"criterion_id":"C1","text":"all evidence accepted", "provenance":"vp-supplied","version":1,"evidence_refs":[]}], "authorization": {"required_grants":["ticket.write"],"actor_scope":"director"}, "links": {"objective_id":"obj-relpack","room":"obj-relpack"}, "priority": 5 } ``` The controller assigns an unused id when `ticket_id` is omitted, validates workflow binding, ownership, acyclic edges and authorization, then atomically writes the TicketRecord and returns `201 {ticket, revision: 1}`. Same `request_id` replays the original response; a different body returns `409 admission_conflict`.
#### `GET /v1/tickets/{ticket_id}` / `chd_ticket_get`
Returns the TicketRecord, current machine-derived allowed transitions, the latest immutable transition event, link consistency flags and `revision`. An unknown or unreadable ticket returns the shared `404 not_found` shape.
#### `PATCH /v1/tickets/{ticket_id}` / `chd_ticket_update`
Request `{request_id, expected_revision, title?, kind?, parent_id?, depends_on?, accountable_owner?, assignees?, watchers?, criteria?, authorization?, links?, priority?}`. The controller checks the principal's family/room grant and governed owner/dependency rules before atomically updating the record, appending an audit event, and returning the new revision. No state transition is implicit in a field update.
#### `POST /v1/tickets/{ticket_id}/transitions` / `chd_ticket_transition`
Request `{request_id, expected_revision, to, reason?, evidence_refs?}`. The controller resolves the ticket's `machine_ref` against `build-spec/state-machines.json`, checks the registered edge, writer and required facts, then atomically writes the new TicketRecord revision, immutable `/chd/ticket/<id>/event/m<seq:012d>` event and audit record. The operation returns `200` with the updated ticket and event. It cannot create a second workflow or bypass the objective/assignment state canon.
#### `GET /v1/tickets` / `chd_ticket_query`
Supports keyset filters `workflow`, `state`, `kind`, `accountable_owner`, `assignee`, `parent_id`, `depends_on`, `room`, `objective_id`, `updated_since`, `inconsistent`, and `limit` (1–500), with `cursor` and `next_cursor`. Results include link consistency flags and the controller revision. The query is the reconciliation input for boardctl exports and restart recovery.
#### `POST /v1/tickets/import` and `GET /v1/tickets/export`
Export returns a read-only JSONL board view. Import matches rows by `ticket_id` (or a registered source alias), reports `added`, `updated`, `conflicts`, and `ignored`, never deletes by absence, and cannot alter state unless an authorized transition request with `expected_revision` is emitted. Conflicting board edits are preserved as reconciliation records; no blind last-writer-wins path exists.
Errors are `400 bad_request`, `401 unauthenticated`, `403 tool_not_granted` or `ticket_transition_not_allowed`, `404 not_found`, `409 ticket_revision_conflict` or `duplicate`, `422 workflow_version_unknown`/`ticket_owner_required`, and `503 duckbrain_unavailable`. Failed validation and failed persistence make no partial TicketRecord, event, audit or link write. Every call is audited with principal, operation, ticket, expected/actual revision and decision.

### 4.10 `POST /v1/workers/dispatch` — managed worker dispatch
This is the only conforming worker-launch operation. The transport is explicitly **foreman → controller → gateway**: the controller brokers the gateway call, owns the shared reservation ledger, and supplies the profile-bound gateway credential. Direct foreman → gateway transport is not authorized in the conformance envelope.
Request (all fields are persisted with the durable request): ```json { "request_id": "wr-20261109-1015-a1b2", "retry_identity": "CRIER-412:worker:wrk-crier-01:attempt:1", "worker": {"agent_id":"wrk-crier-01", "profile":"chd-worker-crier-01"}, "work": {"ticket_id":"CRIER-412", "assignment_id":"a-7", "room":"task-crier-42", "thread_root":41, "send_id":"s-7", "attempt_id":"at-7"}, "instructions": {"body_ref":"/chd/room/task-crier-42/m000000000041", "criteria_ref":"CRIER-412#criteria", "inline_instructions":"bounded text"}, "workspace": {"workdir":"/srv/work/crier-412", "scope":["repo","tmp"]}, "runtime": {"provider":"deepseek", "model":"deepseek-flash", "context_window":160000}, "authorization": {"principal":"foreman-crier", "capability":"worker.dispatch"}, "admission": {"mode":"run_now"} } ```
Validation is authentication → role/capability → ticket/assignment/thread refs → non-default distinct profile → workspace scope → provider/model/context pass-through → shared capacity reservation → gateway dispatch. The response is `202 {"request_id","run_id","state":"queued|admitted|running"}`. The controller persists `request_id`, `run_id`, `retry_identity`, `ticket_id`, `assignment_id`, `send_id`, `attempt_id`, profile, gateway, and authorization path; no CLI launch or inherited foreman environment is permitted.
`GET /v1/workers/runs/{run_id}` returns asynchronous state (`queued`, `admitted`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `uncertain`, `unreachable`), progress heartbeat, result/report reference, and effective profile/config revision. `POST /v1/workers/runs/{run_id}/cancel` records cancellation intent, requests gateway stop, waits for proven stop before releasing capacity, and returns the durable result. Timeout uses the same recovery path. Same `request_id` replays the original `run_id`; a new request with the same `retry_identity`/logical work returns `409 duplicate` with the existing ids.

### 4.11 `POST /v1/assignments` — wake request (`enqueue_only` or `run_now`)
This operation is controller-authenticated and accepts supervisor requests for its assigned foreman and director requests within delegated scope. The scheduler remains authoritative for timed lanes; for immediate requests the controller's bounded admission path owns the same durable per-gateway/per-agent ledger (one atomic reserve, no second counter), with `scheduler_bump_fallback` only when configured. `enqueue_only` always persists and returns `202 {"state":"queued"}` without a gateway call. `run_now` checks authorization, target readiness and shared capacity atomically; at full cap it persists the request and returns `202 {"state":"queued","reason":"at_capacity"}` (or `429 at_capacity` on synchronous callers), never bypassing the cap. Same `request_id` is idempotent; a different id for the same ticket + assignee + open send returns `409 duplicate` with the winning `send_id`/`attempt_id`.
Request fields are `{request_id, retry_identity, ticket_id, assignment_id, room, thread_root, target_agent, target_gateway, admission, instructions_ref, criteria_ref, authorization}`. The target gateway and agent must be ready and have capacity under the shared ledger before an atomic reservation. Timed scheduler and supervisor-triggered requests race on that primitive: under cap 1 exactly one dispatch/attempt wins and the loser receives the winner ids; when full, both remain queued and exactly one dispatch occurs when a slot is proven free. Restart re-derives reservations from manifests, preserving duplicate identity and preventing leaked slots.

## 5. Common error codes
Single public error contract (R31-002/003). This table is identical to VOL-C §3.6 — no second variant exists anywhere (schema, tools, probes). Non-member rule: a room (or agent/report/ticket target) that does not exist **or** is not accessible to the caller yields the identical `404 not_found` status and body shape; the denial cause is recorded only in the authorized audit record (VOLC-064). There is no `403 forbidden` code: agent tokens on VP endpoints are `403 vp_identity_misuse`, and non-member room access is `404 not_found`.
| Status | `error.code` | When | |--------|--------------|------| | 400 | `bad_request` | Malformed body, unknown field, bad limit/pattern | | 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing/invalid token | | 403 | `identity_mismatch` | Body identity ≠ credential (VOLC-001) | | 403 | `kind_not_allowed` | Message-kind legality violation (VOL-C §3.6) | | 403 | `vp_identity_misuse` | Internal agent claiming VP identity — default-deny, counted | | 403 | `approval_required` | Approval gate denied/explicitly refused | | 403 | `policy_resync_not_granted` | Resync without authority | | 403 | `tool_not_granted` | No effective `use` for the operation | | 403 | `assignment_not_grant` | Assignment payload tried to mutate permissions | | 403 | `registry_unjustified` | `space` creation without registry justification (CT-09) | | 404 | `not_found` | Unknown **or** unreadable room/agent/report/ticket — one code, one shape (non-member contract above) | | 409 | `duplicate` | `dedupe_key` replay with differing body | | 409 | `report_already_posted` | Second different report for one (send, attempt) | | 409 | `thread_not_owned` | Reply to a subthread no live bond owns | | 409 | `admission_conflict` | Idempotency key already names other work | | 409 | `ticket_revision_conflict` | Stale `expected_revision` | | 422 | `schema_unsupported` / `schema_validation` / `dataset_row_invalid` | Report v3 schema negotiation, content validation, or typed dataset row failure | | 422 | `attempt_target_conflict` | Reused gateway key against a new target | | 429 | `at_capacity` | Gateway at `max_inflight`; message persisted, wake queued | | 503 | `duckbrain_unavailable` | Store down — sends do not dispatch (§5.3), no verdicts manufactured |

## 6. Endpoint → actor matrix
| Endpoint | VP | director | manager | supervisor | scheduler | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `POST /v1/signals` | ✅ default-allow | ❌ deny | ❌ deny | ❌ deny | n/a | | `POST /v1/cycle` | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (callback credential) | | room ops (create/post/reply/wake/bump/notify) | ✅ | ❌ (via CT-05 room writes) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | `POST /v1/reports/verify` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | `GET /v1/rooms/*/messages` | ✅ | read-only, own rooms | read-only, own rooms | read-only, own rooms | ❌ | | `GET /v1/status` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
Agents post INTO rooms with their role token (CT-05); the router wakes targets (CT-07). They never need these endpoints.

## 7. Endpoint → DuckBrain key-write map
| Endpoint | Keys written | |----------|--------------| | `POST /v1/rooms` | `chd/room/<room-id>/1` | | `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/messages` | `chd/room/<room-id>/<seq>` | | `.../messages/{seq}/replies` | `chd/room/<room-id>/<seq>` (with `thread`) | | `.../messages/{seq}/wake` | none (wake recorded in send manifest) | | `POST /v1/rooms/{room}/bump` | none (scheduler bump only) | | `.../missing-replies/notify` | none (manifest updates only) | | `POST /v1/reports/verify` | `chd/send/<send-id>/manifest` (outcome) | | `POST /v1/signals` | `chd/room/<target_room>/<seq>` + manifest rows | | `POST /v1/cycle` | `chd/send/<send-id>/manifest` per composed send | | config change (startup) | `chd/registry/<agent-id>`, `chd/bond/<agent-id>` — **harness only** |

## 8. Complete operation reference
The endpoint cards and failure branches are authoritative in `build-spec/VOL-E-operation-reference.md` §7. This contract remains the transport-level source for endpoint paths and JSON shapes; VOL-E adds the operation identity, ordered validation, idempotency boundary, storage effects, attachment lifecycle and test cross-link. Every endpoint below is represented there: signals/cycle, room create/post/reply/wake/bump/notify, report verification, room read, ticket CRUD/transition/query/import/export, status, administration, worker dispatch/run control, grants, approvals, archive and profile operations.

### 8.1 Common request/response/error rules
All mutating endpoints accept `request_id` (required, 1–128) and optional `dedupe_key` (1–256); requests are JSON `application/json`, unknown fields fail `400 bad_request`, and mutating success is acknowledged only after fsync. `202` means queued or approval-pending, not completed. Every error code resolves to VOL-E §4; no endpoint invents a private error vocabulary.

### 8.2 Administration and lifecycle endpoint shapes
`POST /v1/admin/bootstrap` accepts `{request_id, schema_version:1, control_namespace:"chd", archive_namespace:"chd-archive"}` and returns `{ok, bootstrap_id, readiness}`. `POST /v1/admin/agents` accepts `{request_id, id, role, profile, gateway, model, context_limit, max_turns, token_budget, skills, tools, rooms}`; `POST /v1/admin/gateways` accepts `{request_id, id, url, transport, auth_token_ref, max_inflight}`. `POST /v1/admin/profiles/{agent}/sync` accepts `{request_id, desired_config_digest, skills:[{name,version,digest}], assets:[{name,digest,content_ref}], rollback_to_config_digest?}` and returns desired/effective digests plus `drifted`. `POST /v1/attachments` accepts `{request_id, content_type, size, digest, transfer:"binary"|"reference", reference?}` and returns a staging `attachment_id`. `POST /v1/attachments/{id}/finalize` accepts `{request_id, digest, size}` and returns a published reference. `POST /v1/attachments/{id}/cleanup` accepts `{request_id, reason}`. Supported content types and limits are exactly VOL-E §3.2; image/PDF binary upload is unsupported and must be a reference. Staging is not readable or linkable.

Grant issue/revoke accepts the GrantRecord lineage and scope fields from VOL-B §3.13; approval resolution accepts `{approval_id, decision:"approved"|"refused", reason, evidence_refs}`. Archive export/restore/read accepts the SessionArchive, ExportManifest, ArchiveGapRecord and explicit selector/grant fields from DATA-MODEL §1.10–§1.11 and VOL-B §3.12/§5.10. The action-specific failure and rollback contract is in VOL-E §7 OP-023–OP-041.
